subject.title: Feature Request: Automated Session Memory Preservation & Synthesis

question: Should reset-time memory preservation and synthesis be owned as bundled OpenClaw behavior, exposed as a memory-plugin lifecycle contract, or deferred to external ClawHub/MCP packages?
rationale: The source shows partial hooks and memory loading already exist, but choosing automatic provider-backed synthesis and durable transcript-derived storage changes privacy, retention, config, and plugin API policy beyond a safe autonomous fix.

options.title: Define a memory-plugin lifecycle contract
options.body: Expose or refine the reset/session-end contract so a memory plugin can do bounded, sanitized synthesis while core owns only the generic lifecycle and safety rules.

options.title: Bundle reset synthesis in core
options.body: Add a first-party reset-time synthesis path, but accept that core must own provider execution, retention, redaction, config, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub/MCP packages
options.body: Keep core unchanged and point users to packages such as world-model-mcp or Agent Capsule, leaving any missing OpenClaw seam to be filed separately.

recommendation.title: Define a memory-plugin lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Expose or refine the reset/session-end contract so a memory plugin can do bounded, sanitized synthesis while core owns only the generic lifecycle and safety rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history owner for the active session-memory/reset-hook implementation and the likely product-boundary decision.
